Figure~\ref{fig:receiver-structure} represents the posterior in
\eqref{eq:working-posterior}.
Following the turbo message-passing framework in \cite{cai2026}, the receiver
iterates between linear estimation and joint denoising.
Information is exchanged between the two estimators through Gaussian
extrinsic messages based on expectation propagation \cite{minka2001}.

text:
To form the extrinsic message, we use a Gaussian approximation with mean
$\widehat X_k$ and common variance $\overline t_X$.
Let $b=\overline t_X/v$.
Dividing this approximation by the incoming Gaussian message, as in
\eqref{eq:linear-extrinsic}, gives
\begin{equation}
 \gamma_{\rm out}=\frac{vb}{1-b},\qquad
 X_{k,\rm out}=\frac{\widehat X_k-bR_k}{1-b}.
 \label{eq:nonlinear-extrinsic}
\end{equation}
For $0<b<1$, the extrinsic variance is positive.
The output means form $\mathbf X^{\rm pri}$, and $\gamma_{\rm out}$ is the
input variance of the linear estimator in the next iteration.

text:
Consider the channel observation under the active hypothesis in
\eqref{eq:pseudo-awgn}.
For a complex-valued channel sample $H\sim q_{\rm tr}$, we stack the
real and imaginary parts of $\vect(H)$ in $\mathbf h_{\mathbb
R}\in\mathbb R^{2D}$.
We add proper complex Gaussian noise with covariance $\mathbf C\succ0$,
independently of $H$.
The real observation is
\begin{equation}
 \begin{gathered}
 \mathbf u=\mathbf h_{\mathbb R}+\bm\Sigma^{1/2}\bm\epsilon,
 \qquad \bm\epsilon\sim\mathcal N(\mathbf0,\I_{2D}),\\
 \bm\Sigma=\frac12
 \begin{bmatrix}\Re \mathbf C&-\Im \mathbf C\\\Im \mathbf C&\Re \mathbf C\end{bmatrix}.
 \end{gathered}
 \label{eq:colored-query}
\end{equation}

We train the denoiser over a range of noise variances
\cite[Sec.~IV-B]{cai2026}.
For training with correlated noise \cite[Sec.~III-B]{shastri2022}, we add
colored Gaussian noise with covariance
$\mathbf C=v(\mathbf R_{\rm a}\otimes\I_N\otimes\mathbf R_{\rm c})$
to clean channel samples and condition the network on $\mathbf C$.
The Kronecker factors follow the antenna--output--input order.
The covariance factors and the sampling distribution of $v$ are specified in
Section~\ref{sec:training-settings}.

Reshaping the real and imaginary outputs of $f_\theta$ defines the
complex-valued denoiser $F_\theta(R,\mathbf C)$.
For the input message in \eqref{eq:pseudo-awgn}, we evaluate
$F_\theta$ at $\mathbf C=v\I_D$.
The network architecture and preconditioning are given in
Section~\ref{sec:network-settings}.

text:
Differentiating \eqref{eq:tweedie-mean} with respect to $\mathbf u$ at fixed
$\mathbf C$ gives the Jacobian $\mathbf J_m=\partial\mathbf
m_{\mathbb R}/\partial\mathbf u =\I_{2D}+\bm\Sigma\nabla_{\mathbf u}^2 \log
q_{\bm\Sigma}^{\mathbb R}(\mathbf u)$.
Right-multiplying by $\bm\Sigma$ and using \eqref{eq:tweedie-covariance}, we
obtain \cite[Prop.~1]{dytso2023}
\begin{equation}
 \mathbf P_{\mathbb R}=\mathbf J_m\bm\Sigma,\qquad
 \tau^\star=\frac1D\tr(\mathbf J_m\bm\Sigma).
 \label{eq:mean-derivative-variance}
\end{equation}
Here $\tau^\star$ is the average conditional variance per complex coordinate.
At $\mathbf C=v\I_D$, this reduces to $\tau^\star=v\operatorname{div}\mathbf
m_{\mathbb R}/(2D)$.

text:
For a Gaussian input $(R_k,v)$, the denoiser gives
$F_k=F_\theta(R_k,v\I_D)$, and the classifier gives $p_k$ in
\eqref{eq:activity-probability}. With
$\widehat\tau_k=\widehat\tau_\theta(R_k,v\I_D)$ from
\eqref{eq:derivative-trace}, we use the common variance estimate
\begin{equation}
 \tau_{\rm raw}=\frac1K\sum_{k=1}^K\widehat\tau_k,\qquad
 \tau^{\rm post}=\max\{\tau_{\rm raw},\tau_{\min}\}.
 \label{eq:pooled-variance}
\end{equation}
Here $\tau_{\min}>0$ is a numerical floor.

Algorithm~1 combines these estimates with $p_k$ and returns Gaussian
extrinsic messages to MFLE. Estimated phases are refined as in
Appendix~\ref{app:phase-refinement}. After normalization,
we initialize $\mathbf X^{{\rm pri},(0)}=\mathbf0$,
$\gamma^{(0)}=\rho\widehat P_H$, $E_k=0$, $c_k=1$, and
$\kappa^{(1)}=1$, where $\widehat P_H$ is the average
of $\norm{H}_F^2/D$ over the training channels.
Stopping checks and numerical settings are given in
Section~\ref{sec:simulation-settings}.

text:
The procedure in Appendix~\ref{app:frontend} estimates the phases used to form
$\widehat{\mathbf A}$, which is fixed between phase refinements.
For noise-variance estimation, let
$\mathbf y_{qr}=(Y_{q0r},\ldots,Y_{q,M-1,r})^{\mathsf T}$ and
$N_{\rm s}=QN>M\geq2$. The spatial sample covariance and noise-variance estimate are
\begin{equation}
 \widehat{\mathbf R}_y=\frac1{N_{\rm s}}\sum_{q,r}
 \mathbf y_{qr}\mathbf y_{qr}^{\mathsf H},\qquad
 \widehat\sigma^2=\frac{\sum_{i=\widehat r_{\rm s}+1}^{M}\lambda_i}
 {M-\widehat r_{\rm s}}.
 \label{eq:noise-estimation}
\end{equation}
Here $\lambda_1\geq\cdots\geq\lambda_M$ are the covariance eigenvalues,
and $\widehat r_{\rm s}$ is selected by the Wax--Kailath minimum
description length (MDL) criterion \cite{wax1985,nadakuditi2008}.
This estimator assumes a low-rank signal covariance and spatially white
noise. We keep the estimate fixed during MP.

With precomputed chirp factors, $L$ AFDM frames require at most
$LC_{\rm FFT}(N)+2LN$ complex multiplications
\cite[eq.~(16)]{bemani2022}, where $C_{\rm FFT}(n)$ is the cost of an
$n$-point FFT or inverse FFT. For the same $LN$ useful symbols,
rectangular-pulse OTFS without transmit windowing requires
$NC_{\rm FFT}(L)$ after cancelling the consecutive DFT and inverse DFT operations
\cite{zou2021otfs}.

text:
For JADCE with fixed phases and $Q\leq KN$, the singular value decomposition
(SVD), $\widehat{\mathbf A}=\mathbf U\diag(s_1,\ldots,s_Q)\mathbf V^{\mathsf H}$,
is reused across iterations, where $s_a$ are the singular values.
The scalar updates in
\eqref{eq:linear-variance}--\eqref{eq:linear-extrinsic} can be written as
\begin{equation}
 f_{\rm L}=\frac{1}{KN}\sum_{a=1}^{Q}
 \frac{\gamma s_a^2}{\widehat\sigma^2+\gamma s_a^2},\qquad
 t_{\rm L}=\gamma(1-f_{\rm L}),\qquad
 v_{\rm L}=\frac{t_{\rm L}}{f_{\rm L}}.
 \label{eq:linear-fraction}
\end{equation}
Here $\mathbf R_{\rm L}=\mathbf X^{\rm pri} +(\mathbf X_{\rm L}-\mathbf
X^{\rm pri})/f_{\rm L}$.
sources: 本文线性矩阵公式的 SVD 计算形式；Rangan VAMP III, (11), Algorithm 2, 作者稿 pp.3–4
note: 独立说明 SVD 复用，外信息表达式接回本段；不是 Cai 的正交导频设计。

text:
SVD and noise-variance estimation cost $O(KNQ^2)$ and $O(QNM^2+M^3)$
per block, respectively. Let $C_{\rm phase}$ denote the phase-search,
refinement, and gain-estimation cost in Appendix~\ref{app:frontend}.
Per iteration, MFLE transformations cost $O(QKMN^2)$, spatial covariance
operations cost $O(KM^2N^2)$, and matrix factorizations cost $O(M^3)$.
Let $C_\theta,C_\phi$ denote the per-device denoiser and classifier costs.
The $1+2L_z$ denoiser evaluations and one classifier evaluation within the
training interval give the per-iteration complexity
\begin{equation}
 \begin{aligned}
 C_{\rm iter}=O\bigl(&QKMN^2+KM^2N^2+M^3\\
 &+K[(1+2L_z)C_\theta+C_\phi]\bigr).
 \end{aligned}
 \label{eq:iteration-complexity}
\end{equation}
For $I$ iterations, the total online complexity is
$O(C_{\rm phase}+QNM^2+M^3+KNQ^2+I C_{\rm iter})$.
Here $C_{\rm phase}=0$ for known phases; each phase refinement also
requires a new $O(KNQ^2)$ SVD. With shared network parameters, the memory requirement
is $O(QKN+KMN^2+KM^2)$ for the pilot matrix and SVD factors, channel messages, and spatial
covariances, excluding parameters and network activations.
